utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The witness may be escorted into the courtroom. The matter you would like to raise, Mr. Traldi, is of such short -- it is about P6659, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I also do understand that you have received an English translation and that the revised translation has been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0324-1848-1 ET. And that you would request that the revised version replace the English translation currently attached to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was only reading the text written by your case manager so therefore I knew that you would agree. And I take it that, Mr. Lukic, the Chamber will grant leave to replace the version but the next question is admission. Is there any objection, apart from the language issue, against admission?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the new version may replace the originally uploaded version and P6659 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. One other very brief matter, if I might.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We have been informed that the Registry searched its physical evidence vault and was unable to locate the B/C/S original of Mr. Kecmanovic's expert report for the Kvocka case, and indeed, the version uploaded under 65 ter 30955 is the only one that appears to be in any of the Tribunal's systems, as best we can tell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber appreciates that everyone, Defence and Prosecution, tried to do its best to locate the expert report, yes, and of course the Registry as well. But matters are as they are now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kecmanovic. Perhaps before you put on your ear-phones I should say dobar dan. No, it's dobro jutro -- no, it's fine, put them on. I was just addressing you before you had put on your ear-phones. Therefore I thought I should do it in your own language, but I leave it to that. Before we continue I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Traldi will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we start by calling up 65 ter 30955, page 31. This is another portion of Mr. Kecmanovic's report for the Kvocka case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: While it's coming up, sir, yesterday you testified that it was your impression that VRS forces randomly shelled Sarajevo from the surrounding hills; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I made a correction regarding that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And for this document, we will have page 31 in the English and the B/C/S lacks that page. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The B/C/S can be removed from the screen, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's page 31 you're asking for?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, and that's the correct page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a part of the report which you drafted; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I have it in B/C/S, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is the portion that we don't have the B/C/S original in the systems. So unless you have it in your possession, we do not have the B/C/S of this section. So if I can ask again, this is a portion of the report that you drafted; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it's undated but it was drafted several years after the war; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you'd spent the intervening years living in Belgrade; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, under the heading, "The Sarajevo tragedy," at the bottom of the page in English, you are discussing the situation of Sarajevo Serbs and you write as follows: "But as soon as the front lines were established around Sarajevo, they actually became victims of a twofold terror. The outside terror of their ethnic kin who randomly showered them with shells from the surrounding hills." And then you make allegations about mistreatment of Serbs in Sarajevo. So my question is: In your report, drafted several years after the war, you presented the random shelling of Sarajevo by VRS forces as a fact, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made a correction regarding that in the previous proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So this report contains your impressions rather than facts about what happened? Or did you believe it when you drafted the report to be a fact?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were my impressions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you also received reports about the heavy shelling of Sarajevo at the Bosnian Presidency; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was something we experienced because I was in Sarajevo. It was not a matter that was dealt with by the reports received by the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I again ask you now to answer the questions. You've stated already that you lived there, that you experienced it. The question now was whether you also received reports about the heavy shelling. It's of no use to say that you experienced it because you've told us that already. It's of no use not to answer the question. The question was whether you also received reports. And this is one of my last warnings. Otherwise, we'll have to really -- we have to take a different route in your testimony. I mean, you came here and we fully acknowledge the importance of your testimony for the Defence but if you refuse to directly answer questions that are put to you, and if you again and again stress what you want to say rather than to answer a question, this might have consequences for the weight to be given to your testimony and even perhaps for whether we want to further hear your testimony. Let that be clear to you. You've stated that you experienced it. Now the question is whether you also received reports. Would you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 30947. Page 1 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, these are -- this is the transcript from the 114th session of the Bosnian Presidency on the 9th of June, 1992. You attended that session; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: On page 1 in both languages, right at the beginning, we see General Halilovic briefing the Presidency and he states --

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Can we go to the very top of the transcript so as to be able to see whether I was present during this session? Because I didn't attend them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, you've just testified that you attended it but if we look at page 10 in the B/C/S version, I think we'll see your name. We don't have a full attendee list here on page 1. And that's your name, Kecmanovic, right between Izetbegovic and Halilovic; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could go back to page 1, General Halilovic states in the second sentence: "First, this artillery fire which was opened at the city during the last 70 hours, non-stop, as far as we were able to work out, at the city of Sarajevo regardless of what devastation results it had, there is a revolt of the people to resist?" Do you see that text?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Artillery fire had been particularly heavy for the few days before the 9th of June; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, the translation is only partial, and the original is complete. I'd propose that we upload as 65 ter 30947A B/C/S version that corresponds to the partial translation and I'd ask that an MFI number be reserved for when we've done that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And if there is any other context need, Mr. Lukic, I take it that you'll make proposals for that purpose. Yes. Madam Registrar, could we reserve a number for what will be an excerpt of the -- of the minutes of the BiH Presidency meeting held on the 9th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Reserve number for document 30947A would be -- is P6660, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to turn to the pre-war political events you discussed during direct examination. You mentioned one specific session of the Bosnian Assembly in paragraph 8 of your statement, the session on 14 and 15 October 1991. Do you recall that session?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not very precisely, although I was in attendance.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you don't mention in your statement that you were there yourself, do you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall precisely whether I attended the whole of the session because I was under no obligation to do so. I could be present, though, without the right of vote, in the capacity of party president.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you say in your statement that your party, afterwards, "said it was against the Muslim-Croat coalition making decisions that contravened the views of the Serbian side." That is all you say in your statement about this Assembly session; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The position of my party was to object one-sided decisions of any of the three sides, in the tripartite bodies of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, it appears you're referring to a two-decided decision, but regardless, my question was: That is all you say about this session in your statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The portion of the statement should be put on the screen so this witness can check. He cannot know by heart the whole statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then of course you need to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the question is whether that's the only thing, then you should put the whole. But I think it would perhaps be good to have the relevant portion on the screen, Mr. Lukic. To that extent I fully agree with you, but it doesn't resolve the problem. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm happy to have that paragraph called up. We need paragraph 8 of D556. And I notice the witness no longer has the B/C/S hard copy that was provided to him yesterday. But I'm happy for him to be provided with a clean one again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then he'll be provided with it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, paragraph 8 is on, I believe, page 4 of the B/C/S. And page 5 of the English.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: 8. So I'll put to you again: It's correct, isn't it, that all you say about this Assembly session is that your party said it was against the Muslim-Croat coalition making decisions that contravened the views of the Serbian side and you explained why you took that position. That's all you say about this session; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the second sentence of this paragraph, you can find what I just referred to. It was in keeping with our principled approach that the three ruling parties must refrain from making any moves on their own. That is to say that a three-way consensus had to be behind all decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Again, that is all you say about this session in your statement; correct? I see you've nodded but you have to articulate your answer for the record.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, Radovan Karadzic also spoke at this session, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Toward the end of the debate, he made a shocking statement that the Muslim people would perish in the war that would be provoked by the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina against the will of the Serbs, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you did not consider that relevant to mention in your statement for this case, did you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was quoted multiple times. It was very well known, and I found it unnecessary to stress that particular fact yet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, just to have the record completely clear, I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to play a clip from P2004. For the record it will start at 9.29 and end at 9.56 of that exhibit. My understanding is the booths have been provided with a transcript of this portion of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you'll put questions to the witness about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because just to look at it, that it happened seems to be not very much in dispute. If it is about the speech delivered by Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to remind the booths, the portion we are playing will start on page 3 in the transcript in both languages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we have to then play it twice, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I believe it was confirmed for when it was played and introduced into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that is the case, we can play it one time only. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "... it is not good what you are doing. This is the road that you want Bosnia and Herzegovina to take, the same highway of hell and suffering that Slovenia and Croatia went through. Don't think you won't take Bosnia and Herzegovina to hell and Muslim people in possible extinction. Because Muslim people will not be able to defend itself if it comes to war here. Please, I know these are serious words."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's the end of the clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I do have some brief questions for you about that clip. First, that's the statement that we were just discussing; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You said yesterday, during direct examination, that Serbs in Bosnia were aware of what happened in Croatia and concerned about the change in the Croatian constitution in 1990. Now, a reference to the highway to hell, and the path to death and destruction that Croatia and Slovenia went through, Muslims and Croats in the Assembly and elsewhere would have been aware of the consequences of the war that by then had broken out in Croatia, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll try to ask it more simply. By the time he gave this speech, Muslims and Croats in Bosnia would have been aware of the consequences of the war in Croatia for the Croatian population there, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For both the Serbs and Croats, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the impact on them of Mr. Karadzic's words would have been, as you described it, shocking, wouldn't it, and terrifying?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present when Karadzic spoke these words, and it was meant to be cautionary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, in that report, you used the word "shocking." The question is whether the impact indeed would be shocking for the population listening to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can say that it was a shocking warning, so as to include both.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And a terrifying one, right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you said in your statement that your party expressed its opposition to making decisions without the consent of one of the constituent peoples. Did your party also express its opposition to the idea of one of the constituent people of Bosnia-Herzegovina perishing in a war?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did not have to do with individual political statements. It had to be applied to the principle of voting and decision-making.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So do I understand your evidence to be that your party, after this shocking statement, took no position on it but opposed what the Muslim and Croat coalition had done at that session; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We opposed one-sided decisions. As for the individual statements of politicians, sometimes we reacted, at other times we did not. It wasn't a matter of principle. We explicitly stood for what we -- what I stated in paragraph 8. We were in favour of all decisions being reached by consensus.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I understand that as a good politician, you're explaining to us your party's principles. What I'm asking is: Did you take a position on this specific statement?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't know. I can't say either way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Bosnian Serbs also formed a separate Assembly in response to what happened at this Assembly session; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you don't mention that in your statement, do you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The establishment of the Assembly, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your party took no position on the forming of a Serb Assembly, did it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We considered that to be a logical consequence of the outvoting that happened in the joint parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you, yourself, attended the founding session of that Assembly; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as a guest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And a plebiscite, as you testified about yesterday, was also organised in response to what had happened on the 14th and 15th; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you didn't oppose that plebiscite; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean personally or as a party?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As a party.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you're aware, aren't you, that Serbs and non-Serbs were issued different coloured ballots?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I can't really say either way. If you'll allow me, I would like to give a brief explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At the moment, I'm interested in the question I've just asked.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so let's pull up 65 ter 07941.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the English translation is not released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I believe we are in the process of remedying that, Your Honour. I just ask your indulgence for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm told it's been released now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because it was on your list, so therefore it's to be expected, but we now have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so we can see the original on the left side in blue; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And could we have 65 ter 07942?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: English translation not released, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we can see this ballot in yellow; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we can also see without going through it in detail that there is different text on this ballot, that there is less text on this ballot than the one before; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just read what it says here on this yellow paper. Could you please return the other ballot, the white or blue one, the red or blue one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The blue is 07941. There is more text on this one by comparison; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we have the English translation back? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And for instance, the references to the Serb people in this blue ballot are absent from the yellow ballot that we just looked at, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd put to you that these different coloured ballots in the plebiscite were also not mentioned in your statement; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd put to you that this was widely known at the time. You were a member of and active in Bosnian politics, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you know Radovan Karadzic was asked about this on video?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, the last question and answer are ambiguous. You did put to the witness that this, being the two different ballot papers, was widely known at the time. Witness, when you answered yes, did you acknowledge that this was widely known at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know about it. Now, if it was widely known, I would assume that I would have supposed to have known it but I wasn't aware of these two different ballots.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the answer to the first part of the question is: I couldn't tell you. And the answer to the second part, then, must be about a yes that you were a member of an active -- you were active in Bosnian politics. You confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, did you know that Mr. Karadzic was interviewed about the plebiscite, including about the different coloured ballots?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can I take it that you also don't remember your party taking any position on the plebiscite being administered differently to members of different ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps now would be a good moment for me to describe briefly what my party did, the party that I led, and our position on the plebiscite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we would like you to answer the question. If at the very end there is any need to address any matter which is directly related to a question, you have an opportunity to do so, but at this moment, you're invited to focus on the question put to you by Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Would it be useful for me to ask that question again?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can I take it that you also don't remember your party taking any position on the plebiscite being administered differently to members of different ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm certain that we did not take any position on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender these two ballots, 65 ter 07941 and 07942.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under one number or two numbers? Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 7941 receives number P6661 and document 7942 receives number P6662, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6661 and P6662 are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Around this time, Serbian autonomous regions were also declared; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you mentioned this on direct examination, but it's not in your statement either; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You did, at the time, however, publicly express concern about the establishment of SAOs in areas where Serbs were a minority because you believed those would lead to interethnic tensions, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, your party, the SRSJ, was one of several multi-ethnic political parties in Bosnia; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your policies put you in opposition to all the ethnic nationalist parties, the Serbian SDS, Croatian HDZ, and Muslim SDA; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You discuss one of those, the SDA, in detail in your statement and you were asked about them again during direct examination. By the time of the elections in 1990, however, all three parties were essentially mono-ethnic and running on nationalist platforms; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And ethnic nationalism was already a political force in the former Yugoslavia before that, in all three ethnic communities?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You talked about Muslim nationalism a bit during direct examination. I'll just look at one example of Serb nationalism out of many. Vojislav Seselj, who studied at the University of Sarajevo while you were on the faculty, had become a prominent nationalist figure by this time, hadn't he?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 30965? This is an interview with Mr. Seselj as reprinted in one of his books, "Politics as a challenge to the conscience." And the interview is dated 1989, the 18th of April. Once it's come up I'll ask for page 6 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see in the middle of the page in both languages someone represented with the initials MN ask Seselj how the state should be created. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, turning to page 7 in the English, and I believe also in the B/C/S, in the last paragraph before the initials NN appear at the next question, Mr. Seselj opines on the borders of Serbia and he says: "The present core Serbia, Vojvodina, Kosovo and Metohija, Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina" --

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies. Where can I find that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The top of the page in the B/C/S, second sentence.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll start again. "The present core Serbia, Vojvodina, Kosovo and Metohija, Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Macedonia, Dubrovnik, Dalmatia, Lika, Kordun, Banija, Eastern Slavonia and Baranja, should all be within the borders of Serbia." This is nationalist rhetoric; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you mentioned the reaction that you thought Serbs had had to the republishing of the Islamic Declaration. Now, the Islamic Declaration doesn't mention Bosnia and Herzegovina, does it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, on the other hand, mentions Bosnia and Herzegovina and says it should be part of Serbia; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 30965.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I didn't look yet whether this is an excerpt or I take it it's not the whole of the book?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, no, no. It's this interview. It's an excerpt from a chapter as I recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see it's 7 pages in English. Mr. Lukic, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30965 receives number P6663, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6663 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn now to the Cutileiro Plan, and you were familiar with that; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You attended meetings chaired by Mr. Cutileiro in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of them. From time to time my party was invited to join the talks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you attended some of the meetings held in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You did not, however, attend the sessions of the committee in Lisbon; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was supposed to travel to Lisbon. However, the flight was cancelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you did not attend the session; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Lisbon, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 30951? This is an opinion piece written by Mr. Kecmanovic on 26 February 1992. And we'll zoom in on the bottom left-hand part of the page in the B/C/S. I'm looking at the end of the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At the time, you wrote as follows: "The Lisbon proposal will not, as claimed by some, destroy the sovereignty of BH. Instead it is the most realistic way of ensuring its stability. The radical circles of the SDS are seeking to sever parts of BH with the predominantly Serbian population from the republic and establish new states."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can the B/C/S be enlarged with respect to the first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you can see SDS and BiH right above each other on the left-hand side. I'm reading around that portion. So I'll stop there for a moment. It's correct that the SDS was, in your view at the time, seeking to establish new states; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only make reference to some extreme examples but not as the fundamental policies of any party.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Who do you see as representing those extreme examples in the SDS?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot single anyone out, but I know that they -- there were some radical solutions in their discussions within the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 30951.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30951 receives number P6664, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Mr. Traldi, will you follow up on this, on extreme or is it -- have you done with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I have just one follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, then we'll wait for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you refer to discussions within the party. You weren't a member of the SDS; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And weren't privy to those discussions?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, of course not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you're not sure who took which side of those discussions?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think -- I'm not certain but as far as I can remember, I think that Mr. Karadzic himself or perhaps Mr. Koljevic, the late Mr. Koljevic, mentioned at some point that there were such relations within the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, that completes my questions about the topic, if Your Honour had additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said it was the radical fraction within that party. Now, could you tell us where you found that the mainstream opinion in the party was that -- was different from what you describe here as the radical position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The official policy of the Serbian Democratic Party, and that was the dominant position, was to support the Lisbon solution. The Lisbon treaty or agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did that remain over time? Or -- I mean that no new states should be established.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the continuous policies from Lisbon to the Dayton Accords that were also signed by the Serb side as well as the other two, the Croatian and the Bosniak side, support for a common state with entities, cantons and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd like to look at Lisbon in a little more detail. The central issue of the Cutileiro discussions was the effort to ethnically divide Bosnia and Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were aware then that the Bosnian Serbs were seeking an ethnic division of the territory; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In fact, this was a matter of public discussion and everyone was aware of it; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this time, there was -- there were discussions in the political circles in Sarajevo, also outside of the Lisbon talks, there were talks between the parties directly. Simply put, that was the topic of the day: How to divide Bosnia and yet keep it integral and whole. And there were various combinations as to how to accomplish that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you subsequently became aware that the position of the Bosnian Serbs at that time was that they couldn't live with the Muslims, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the clashes that went on for a long time, this was not easily resolved and this was simply the consequence of what preceded it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you did subsequently become aware that that was the Bosnian Serbs' position; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a reaction, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you said earlier that the Serb side had signed and supported the Cutileiro Plan. Did you mean the plan as it was on the 18th of March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the primary desire of the Serbian people and the Serbian Democratic Party as well as my party was to remain in Yugoslavia. However, as that was impossible and there was no tripartite agreement, the Lisbon agreement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll put the question to you again. When you said earlier that the Serb side had signed and supported the Cutileiro Plan, were you referring to the plan as it was on the 18th of March, 1992? Would you please answer that question that was put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot answer that question precisely. When you mentioned the date, does that mean that there were changes in this agreement? Or -- I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's a fair matter, Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm referring to the date that it was discussed in the Serb Assembly which I think you're aware of and has been discussed with you in all your previous testimonies. Did you mean that the Serb side signed and supported the plan as it existed on that date?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date confuses me, but otherwise, yes, there was support for the Lisbon agreement. That is precisely why I asked you if there were different versions of the agreement. I know, generally speaking, that the Lisbon agreement was supported by the SDS and the other two sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to test your evidence in that respect, but looking at the clock, I see I may have to do it after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You certainly will have to do it after the break. Mr. Kecmanovic, we take a break of 20 minutes, and you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. President, while the witness is exiting I can inform the Chamber 65 ter 30947A is now in e-court. It's been provisionally marked as P6660.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic -- and you tender it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I do, although if Mr. Lukic would like to wait until after the break to give his position, I wouldn't oppose that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll use the break to check it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to come in, Mr. Lukic, I think yesterday we cut shorter the time limit for a response to the tu quoque submissions made by the Prosecution mainly because one of the witnesses would appear pretty soon. Therefore we changed it from Wednesday to Monday. I do understand that the Prosecution has now withdrawn in relation to that witness, at least, the tu quoque objection. So therefore for the other witness, where there is no withdrawal or no withdrawal yet, I do not know, the time limit is Wednesday now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Before the witness is with us, I went through the excerpt that has number P6660 and I -- Mr. Traldi and I agreed that I have no objection for admission in this form, but we also agreed that I could add anything I deem necessary. So already I can see that I will ask for another two pages. So I don't know if we should wait until that translation is ready or it should be different number but I think it's not the best idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm happy to wait until the translation is received. Of course, we will want to look it over at that point. Will the Defence be putting in the request for the translation? We are happy to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That offer is accepted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, on behalf of the Defence you will ask. Mr. Kecmanovic, we will continue with the cross-examination, at least Mr. Traldi will. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, first, to explain the focus on the date of 18 March, that's the date you mention in your statement when the Cutileiro Plan was presented to the RS Assembly by Mr. Karadzic; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember precisely, but most likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just for clarity, perhaps if we could have -- I believe it's paragraph 55 of the witness's statement, D556. The English is on page 22. And I see the B/C/S has already been located.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So in paragraph 55, you give that date; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have P4582? This will be Radovan Karadzic's speech at the 42nd session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly. I'll be looking for page 6 in the English and the bottom of page 4 in the B/C/S. And what he says is: "On 18 March" -- begins in the middle of the page in the English. "On 18 March we won the battle for" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Where is it in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page, as I said, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I missed that, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's all right. "On 18 March we won the battle for our republic. We won it on 18 March, thanks to the skill of Mr. Krajisnik." And he gives some additional details. And then three lines from the bottom, and turning to the top of page 5 in the B/C/S, ten lines from the top exactly, he says: "Then Alija said yes to three Bosnias for the first time and that it would be an ethnic basis and that was fatal for him. They showed us completely unacceptable maps but Cutileiro said you can accept this as a basis for further discussion. Then we" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move to the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. "Then we seized it with both hands, yes, as a basis for further discussion, yes. It was important to us that it was in three, that it was on a territorial basis, and that there was some kind of map in existence by which we could establish our right to territory as between 45 and 50 per cent, you know what Cutileiro's map looked like. Then Bosnia exploded, then we were accepted as a side in the conflict. The international community made a serious mistake because they sent Cutileiro and Carrington to us before the war because they accepted us as a side in the conflict. If they had ignored us and kept quiet, recognised Bosnia and said afterwards that there was some kind of insurrectionists there who were wrecking their own state, we would be in serious difficulties, nobody would be talking to us."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, that's a lengthy excerpt but I'll have a few specific questions for you about it. First, Mr. Karadzic is clear that the Bosnian Serb leadership found the maps attached to the Cutileiro Plan completely unacceptable; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And had no intention of accepting those maps as they were; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: He's saying, I'd put to you, that the Bosnian Serbs' goal was to use the plan to lock in their right to a separate ethnic entity while subsequently seeking control of more territory than was granted them in the plan. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the same percentage as contained in the Dayton Accords, between 45 and 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, that wasn't the question. Would you please answer the question? Mr. Traldi will repeat it if you ask him to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd put to you that Mr. Karadzic is saying that the Bosnian Serbs' goal was to use the plan to lock in their right to a separate ethnic entity while subsequently seeking control of more territory than was granted them in the plan. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, that's a different picture of their position on the Cutileiro Plan than the one you paint in your statement, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated what the general position was vis-à-vis the Cutileiro Plan rather than discussing any territorial details.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Bosnian Serb leadership at this -- at the time of the plan, 18th of March, already claimed territory which went beyond the territory they would have been granted by the Cutileiro Plan; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's look at P4580. This is the record of the 11th session of the RS Assembly, dated the 18th of March. I'm going to ask that we turn to page 10 in the English and 12 in the B/C/S. Sorry, to 38 in the English and 56 in the B/C/S. Do we have both? At the bottom of the page, in the English -- I'm not certain where it appears in the B/C/S. I see a 54 on the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That seems to -- I saw a reference to Bosanska Krupa on the page we previously had on our screen. It was the second paragraph. I might be mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I strongly suspect Your Honour is correct, then. Yes. Exactly, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So what Mr. Vjestica says, speaking of his own municipality, is: "Bosanska Krupa is a textbook example, it's been six months now since the current MUP, inspections or other services have not been to our Serbian territories around Mount Grmic, into this area of Serbian municipalities. They cannot, we do not let them. They do not dare to. We have de facto occupied our own territories." And we will turn to the next page in English. "But here, we must reach an agreement that all Serbs, in all municipalities, both the newly formed and the existing ones, take over the power because we have not taken over. Mr. President, I think that you have to give us an order, that after the next session of the Assembly you should order this, that we arrange it for the areas where it has not been done and to implement this, that the Serbs should occupy their territories so that no other forces could enter them. Thank you." And then it reflects there is applause. So that municipality, Bosanska Krupa --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry for interrupting. I'm on B/C/S channel now and there is really a wrong typo, typo mistake in this text, and the translators are reading it that way. It says "dvoje" and it has no sense. It should be "svoje" so the Professor is not confused. Or as it is translated in English, "Our territories."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it is an obvious mistake, Mr. Lukic, we appreciate --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because "dvoje" also has a meaning so it's not obvious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's not obvious you shouldn't have discussed it in the presence of the witness. That's the reason why I'm saying that. You consider the original B/C/S to be -- to contain a typo where it says "svoje" -- no --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Dvoje."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could I just ask that the witness take the headphones off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness may well understand the English language. You take off your ear-phones.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not a big issue. I just do not want this witness to be confused. "Dvoje" means "both," "svoje" means "our." So he could get the impression that somebody wants to take two territories, both territories. And "svoje" means "our" territory. So if it's translated into English as "svoje," I think it's correct. But still it was read the way it was written in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that the last two words of the previous paragraph do say "svoje" territory. Because we started reading at the Bosanska Krupa school example, I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yeah, "skolski primjer."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In both paragraphs. First paragraph that was read, three lines from the bottom of that paragraph, on the left-hand side, it says, "dvoje teritorija." And the same in the next paragraph, second line from the bottom, also says, "dvoje teritorija."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and in the previous paragraph, it says, "svoje teritorija," last two words.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right, but that paragraph, I don't know if it's read out or not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it was not read out but the following paragraph was not -- yes, was read out. But should occupy, you say, our territories. Is that what you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's logical as it was translated into English but the witness should hear the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I think the meaning would be, if you occupied their territories you make it your territory but the claim is that they are our territories already and now to be occupied by the Serbs. That's -- I think the meaning is not that much different although differently phrased.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm happy to read it as I initially did and have the booth translate my words to the witness if that would be agreeable to Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it's the last sentence before the word "applause," sir. So that last sentence reads from the beginning --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only the witness has to have his headphones --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has to put his earphones on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Of course, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We had a small linguistic problem, Mr. Kecmanovic. Mr. Traldi will now continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to reread that sentence. It begins: "Mr. President, I think that you have to give us an order that after the next session of the Assembly you should order this, that we arrange it for the areas where it has not been done and to implement this, that the Serbs should occupy their territories so that no other forces could enter them. Thank you." And then it reflects applause. Now, Mr. Vjestica's own municipality, Bosanska Krupa, was not granted to the Bosnian Serbs by the Cutileiro Plan, was it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really not aware of such territorial details of the Cutileiro Plan, at least not precisely. I don't know whether Bosanska Krupa was made part of it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, could we have 65 ter 30950? And this is a map colour coded to represent the Cutileiro Plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any disagreement about the matter between Prosecution and Defence? Bosanska Krupa not to be Serb in the Cutileiro Plan because otherwise we just put it to the witness if the parties agree on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to go through the map in a little more detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid that I don't know the Cutileiro Plan that well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed then as you suggested.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So if we look to the northwest, Bosanska Krupa bears the colour code for a Muslim area; right? You can see on the legend that the pale colour is for Muslim areas?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Prijedor and Sanski Most are also colour coded for Muslim areas; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to the southeast of there, can you see Donji Vakuf also colour coded for a Muslim area? Just south of Jajce and east of Kupres and Sipovo?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And looking to the east of the country, along the Drina River, Zvornik, Vlasenica, Bratunac, Visegrad, Srebrenica, Rogatica, and Foca, those are all colour coded as Muslim areas; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Are you familiar with an area known as the Posavina corridor?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Posavina corridor is not entirely coded red for a Serb area, is it? There are portions colour coded for Muslim and then some municipalities that are blue for Croat?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the areas I just mentioned were all claimed by the Bosnian Serbs, though; right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness, he is speaking off mike.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please speak into the microphone? The interpreters can't hear you. And repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the document you quoted a moment ago, there is only a reference to Bosanska Krupa.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I understand that. I also know that you're aware of the Serb autonomous regions that had been declared at this time. And I'd put to you that the regions I just mentioned, with a couple of exceptions, are part of those Serb autonomous regions and were all part of the Serbs' territorial claims. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And for the Chamber's reference, the SAOs are reflected in P3930 and a map at P178, page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, the Chamber has received evidence that the Bosnian Serbs took control of almost all of the areas I just mentioned during 1992, many of them as early as April 1992. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was that before or after the Cutileiro Plan which was rejected by the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's after the Cutileiro Plan. After the 18th of March.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After it was rejected?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you're here to testify. What's your evidence as to when you say the Muslim side withdrew from the Cutileiro Plan?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was trying to say the following: Any territorial changes as compared to the Cutileiro Plan occurred after it was rejected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, carefully listen to the question. When do you say the Muslim side withdrew from the Cutileiro Plan? That was the question. Would you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know when precisely but upon return from Lisbon, after it was initialled.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So I'd put this as April 1992. The Cutileiro Plan, we have explained, Karadzic presented to the Assembly on the 18th of March. But I'd put to you again that many of these territories were taken over by the Bosnian Serbs as early as April 1992. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In fact, yesterday you testified that the Bosnian mobilisation on the 4th of April, 1992, had "practically meant introducing war into Bosnia and Herzegovina." Fighting had already broken out, including in Bijeljina, before that, hadn't it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so it's not true, is it, to say that war was introduced to a place where the war had already started?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There had been local skirmishes before, but I wanted to say that in general terms, war broke out in Bosnia after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only -- sorry, only one thing. I don't know if it's only me, but I can see on the left, top left corner, for four municipalities different colour, like greenish, Velika Kladusa, Cazin, Bihac, Bosanska Krupa. So is there any explanation for that on this map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, it seems to be right and even in the legend it seems lightly greenish as well, but isn't this specifically a matter the parties could agree on? I take it that maps to the Cutileiro Plan are somewhere in official documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: There is one already in evidence. It's harder to work with visually on the screen which is why I've used this one but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And greenish and white here is the same for you and is at least not red and not blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I agree that both green and white are neither red nor blue. If Mr. Lukic would like, I can refer him to the one that's in evidence, somewhat harder to work with, and he can double check that it corresponds and we can come back to the matter. If that would suit everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic, the Chamber will admit this map into evidence but you're free to revisit the matter if the green and white causes problems of substance. Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30950 receives number P6665, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6665 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And for Mr. Lukic's reference, the map to which I referred is at Exhibit P3106, page 4. And came in as an associated exhibit to the evidence of Witness Okun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to turn now, sir, to three meetings you mention in your statement which occurred soon after the failure of the Cutileiro Plan. First, a meeting at the Terme Hotel, and for reference this is discussed at paragraph 16 of your statement. Do you recall that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a long time ago but I do remember in general terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So I have just simple questions for you about this. Nothing specific was discussed at that meeting by way of plans or proposals that might have achieved peace, was it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is your answer that I'm correct that nothing specific was discussed at that meeting that might have achieved peace? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And nothing of value came out of that meeting, did it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And next, you discuss a meeting between Mr. Izetbegovic and Mr. Krajisnik about dividing Sarajevo so that Muslims would control the city centre and Serbs would control the suburbs. Do you recall that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Mr. Koljevic, who you mention in your statement, told you that Mr. Karadzic had also agreed to the plan discussed at that meeting; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And he would have had to due to his role; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask now that Ms. Stewart play a clip from "Death of Yugoslavia" and that we look at how Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Izetbegovic described the meeting. That's 65 ter 30851A. I understand the translation has been confirmed by CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that's the case, we can play it once.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Izetbegovic: When the cannons above the city started pounding, when the destruction of the city was under way, Krajisnik offered that we meet, to strike a deal on Sarajevo, as he put it." [In English] "Anchor: They chose the now abandoned parliament building for their secret talk." [Interpretation] "Krajisnik: I arrived first. It was already dark. "Izetbegovic: Before this, we were friends, in a way. We were like friends because we had worked together in the parliament for some time before that. "Krajisnik: Then I saw their security men. They had automatic rifles with silencers or something like that, and I said: 'Is that what you call a gun? The Serbs are much better equipped.' I was just trying to be funny. "Izetbegovic: He told me: There is no way to avoid dividing the city. "Krajisnik: We had always been thinking about dividing Sarajevo so Muslims had their part and the Serbs theirs. This is no secret. "Izetbegovic: I did not accept the division. I turned him down. We said goodbye and he gave me a pen as a memento."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Krajisnik is clear there that the Serbs always intended to divide Sarajevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I wouldn't say that he said that they always had that intention. It was only in those conditions, the wartime conditions, that were then a reality in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you would agree with me that by the time of this meeting, the Serbs intended to divide Sarajevo; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a proposal put forth by Krajisnik, put forth to Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And then, yes, they clearly had that intent, right, if they were proposing it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The intention was ad hoc, it had to do with a situation in which we were all -- in which we found ourselves, the wartime condition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, could we have the transcription of the video footage on our screen so that if the witness says this is not what Krajisnik said, that we with verify that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And by rephrasing your question, I understood that to be a confirmation of the correct understanding of the witness of what was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It was my attempt to move efficiently, Mr. President, and focus on what I was interested in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If it's just for practical purposes then we -- okay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If you look at the bottom, Mr. Krajisnik says: "We had had always been thinking about dividing Sarajevo." So that's the text that he actually speaks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that's the text that the interpreters read during the video.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we are agreed, too, I think, that by the time of this meeting, the Serbs intended to divide Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps there is miscommunication here. There was a front line around the Sarajevo -- around Sarajevo, and Krajisnik's proposal was to maintain that situation until the Bosnia-Herzegovina situation is finally resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not suggesting -- I'm not asking you about which part would be under the control of the Muslims and which part would be under the control of the Serbs. What I'm asking you is what Mr. Krajisnik clearly says in this video, and what you've said was his proposal at that time, that was what the Bosnian Serb leadership intended at that time; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this clip 65 ter 30851A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30851A receives number P6666, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6666 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As for the third meeting you mention in your statement, that was at Lukavica, and you discussed with Momcilo Krajisnik whether you should join the Izetbegovic Presidency. That's correct too, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you don't mention this in your statements but Mr. Koljevic called your home the evening before you were supposed to join the Presidency; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember talking with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 30941?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I think I'd suggest to you, maybe it would refresh your recollection, if you weren't at home at the time and he spoke to your wife. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that he spoke with some member of my family. The phone lines were on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could I have page 142 of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is your testimony in the Krajisnik case. Now, the eve of your entry into the Presidency, that would have been around the 31st of May, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, reading starting at line 11, you're testifying, and you say: "I'm reminding you of this and what I said yesterday. When you read this out, I happened to remember, for example, that on the eve of my entry into the Presidency, becoming a member of the Presidency, Nikola Koljevic called up by phone but didn't find me at home, so he talked to my wife. He told her that it wouldn't be a good idea; quite the contrary, it would be bad thing if I were to join the Presidency, that that would be a great detriment to the Serb people. My wife recounted that conversation ..." I take it she recounted the conversation to you and that's how you learned of it; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you stand by your testimony in this respect, given in the Krajisnik case?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So Mr. Koljevic did call and say it would be bad for the Serb people if you joined the Izetbegovic Presidency?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That was for public relations reasons essentially; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, you were -- he was concerned, wasn't he, that it would enable the Izetbegovic Presidency to portray itself as a multi-ethnic institution that had Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat and Bosnian Serb members; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Presidency -- I'm done with this testimony now. The Izetbegovic Presidency discussed, in your presence, the problem of people being expelled from the territories where they lived by force, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can 65 ter 30944 be called to our screens? It's an excerpt from the transcript of the 128th BH Presidency session dated the 24th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You attended that session; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please just check on top of the page? You can see whether I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think the top of the page again doesn't have a list of attendees, but if we turn to page 3 in the English and 4 in the B/C/S I think we might find your name. You'll see it's second or third down, rather, on each page. Between Pelivan and Pelivan. Do you see your name?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see here Mr. Akmadzic discussing prerequisites, at the top he's clearly discussing negotiations that lead to peace, and then below your name he says: "There are prerequisites which are cease of war operations, recognition of the single system of government, and negotiations which have as their foundation the creation of pure ethnic territories cannot be accepted." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So the Presidency is discussing avoiding the creation of pure ethnic territories?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, to be fair, turning to the next page in both languages, you take part in the discussion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look at that page?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you propose a particular formulation: "That begins with the pre-war situation in respect of that picture or national structure, the demographic structure in BiH, that this be the starting point and not some that no changes of any kind will be accepted in the national structure of the population that have been produced by war, moving away, et cetera." That was your proposal; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you responded with this formulation because you were aware at this point that there had been changes in the national structure of the population; correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On all three sides, a lot of people had left Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And changes on all three sides that had been produced by war; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And by people moving away in fear of that war and of other things that were happening at the time?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we turn to the next page in both languages, please? We see there is more discussion, and at the very bottom of the page in English, Mr. Izetbegovic says: "So this provision needs to be woven in somewhere, about non-acceptance," and then we will turn to the next page in English, "of any -- any change to the demographic picture, to the demographic situation that were created by war." And you respond below it: "Those are territorial ethnic changes caused by violence, war, genocide, moving away, et cetera." And again, you were aware that changes in the ethnic structure of Bosnia's population were occurring for all those reasons; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This quote, I believe, is incorrect and I can tell because the reference to Halil -- there is a reference to Halil which would refer to General Halilovic and that's not the way that I called him or addressed him. This must have been what Izetbegovic said because he used that form to address him. However, it doesn't really differ much from the earlier quotes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think you're reading a different quote of yours. I direct your attention to the bottom of the page. Do you see what you've said there? "Those are territorial ethnic changes caused by violence, war, genocide, moving away, et cetera."

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] That's you speaking, right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you knew at that time that changes in the ethnic makeup of Bosnia and Herzegovina were happening for all those reasons?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you'd received reports in the Presidency that people were moving out, Muslims and Croats were moving out of Serb-claimed territories for all those reasons; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KECMANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew directly only the fact that Serbs were trying to flee Sarajevo, and as for the other thing, I knew that indirectly through reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you're speaking of territorial ethnic changes. You've said in your statement that Serbs were being stopped from leaving Sarajevo.
